en.name: Cosmas
en.summary: Early physician-martyr who, with his twin brother Damian, treated the sick without payment and became one of the most venerated healing saints in Christian history.
en.body: Cosmas and his twin brother Damian were, by tradition, physicians of Arab origin practicing in the Roman province of Syria in the early fourth century, known throughout their region for treating patients, human and reportedly animal alike, entirely free of charge, earning them the title "unmercenary healers" in Eastern Christian tradition. Their refusal of payment and evident medical skill drew large numbers of patients and, with them, converts to Christianity, which brought them to the attention of authorities during the persecution under Diocletian; after surviving several attempted executions by drowning, fire, and stoning that reportedly failed miraculously, they were finally beheaded around 287. Their cult spread rapidly through both the Eastern and Western Church, and they became patrons invoked for healing across the medieval world, their names included in the Roman Canon of the Mass alongside the apostles and other early martyrs. Their shared feast continues to be marked with particular devotion among the medical profession.
